title.narrative: Road Corridor Investment Program - Tranche 3 (Additional Financing)

description.narrative: The Project, financed from the multitranche finance facility (MFF) for Georgia Road Corridor Investment Program, provides additional financing of $140 million for Loan 2560-GEO (the original project). Its main components are: (i) constructing Kobuleti Bypass (a new 28 km two-lane bypass road skirting Kobuleti and expanding to four lanes, a 6 km section of an existing two-lane road between Kobuleti and Batumi, along the Black Sea coast toward the Turkish border); (ii) strengthening asset management capacity of the Roads Department; and (iii) improving road safety. The additional financing will be used for expenditures related to civil works (road construction component), consulting services for construction supervision, and project administration by the executing agency.

Output: Strengthening of asset management capacity Indicator: Roads Department adopts performance-based contracting for maintenance of at least 100 km of local or national roads Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: It was agreed to proceed with a scope covering both the RAMS training for this project and the PBM component to be carried out under the Batumi Bypass Road Project (L3520-GEO) as well as an additional scope on bridge maintenance, iRAP and national tolling strategy.
A national Road Asset Management Specialist (RAMS) consultant was engaged on 11 Dec 2018 (contract partly financed from L3520-GEO). The draft inception report and work plan were discussed during the Jan/Feb review mission.
The consultant has prepared an estimated timeline of design works which will be aligned with the performance-based maintenance (PBM) consultants' assignment duration to be recruited under L3520-GEO. Data Source: Roads Department surveys

Output: A 33.6 km two-lane bypass road detouring Kobuleti Indicator: The road after construction meets the standards and specifications in the contract document Achievement: Y Progress/Status: All works in Lot 1 (km 0 to 12.4 and km 30 to 33) are completed and all sections are open to traffic.
Lot 2 (km 12.4 - km 31.2) main construction works have been completed and the project road was opened to traffic on 25 June 2018. The Taking Over Certificate was issued in August 2018.
The final report on LARP implementation was submitted to ADB and disclosed on ADB website in December 2018.
The defects notification period (DNP) has been extended until 31 March 2020. The loan was closed on 29 September 2019. Any expenditures incurred after the loan closing date will be financed by the government.
The DNP for Lot 2 construction works was completed on 25 March 2020.
The DNP for Lot 1 road lighting works was completed on 15 May 2020.
The DNP for Lot 2 road lighting works will be completed on 18 December 2020. Upon Expiration of the Engineer's Contract on 31 May 2020, the Roads Department of Georgia will act as the Supervision Engineer for the mentioned works. Data Source: Roads Department surveys
